records.title: Brake Seizure and Uneven Pad Wear
records.description: Because the Twizy is light, uses regenerative braking, and is often driven short distances, its friction brakes can corrode from lack of use. Owners commonly report sticking calipers, seized slide pins, dragging brakes, and uneven pad wear, especially after storage or wet-weather use.
records.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor condition, caliper piston movement, and slide pin lubrication on all corners. Repairs usually involve cleaning and lubricating hardware, replacing seized pins or calipers, and fitting new pads/rotors if corrosion is advanced; expect about $150-$350 for service work, or $300-$700 if calipers and discs are needed.
symptoms: Reduced efficiency or increased rolling resistance

communityRecommendations.content: Use the friction brakes firmly from time to time to keep the discs clean, since regen alone can let corrosion build up.
Owners generally prefer branded pads and hardware kits because cheap friction parts can squeal and corrode quickly on lightly used EV brakes.
If the Twizy is stored, move it periodically and release/reapply the parking brake to reduce sticking.

claims.content: Owners generally prefer branded pads and hardware kits because cheap friction parts can squeal and corrode quickly on lightly used EV brakes.

records.title: 0.9/1.2 TCe Timing Chain Premature Stretch and Tensioner/Guide Failure
records.description: Both the 0.9 TCe 90 (H4Bt) and 1.2 TCe 120 (H5Ft) petrol engines use a nominally 'lifetime' timing chain that in practice can stretch prematurely from around 80,000-100,000 km, with weak tensioners and plastic guides that crack or snap. A contributing root cause is the small oil jet that lubricates the chain, which clogs with soot when oil changes are stretched, accelerating chain and sprocket wear. Owners on UK forums report rattles followed by snapped guides and slipped chains, which can leave the car a non-starter or cause valve damage.
records.solution: Replace the complete timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets) at the first sign of rattle, and verify the chain oil jet is clear during the job. Strict, shortened oil change intervals with the correct specification oil are the accepted prevention; Renault has contributed goodwill (e.g. 75%) on some out-of-warranty failures.
symptoms: Metallic rattle from the engine on cold start
Ticking/rattling from the timing cover area that worsens with revs
Loss of power accompanied by engine warning light
Engine cranks but won't start after chain slips

records.title: 1.2 TCe (H5Ft) Excessive Oil Consumption — "Motorgate" Piston Ring Defect
records.description: Captur I models with the 1.2 TCe 120 (H5Ft) engine built between 2012 and mid-2016 suffer a manufacturing defect: tolerances between the pistons, piston rings and cylinder walls are too wide, letting engine oil pass into the combustion chamber and burn. Affected cars can consume 1 litre of oil per 1,000-1,500 km, fouling the catalytic converter and exhaust valves, and in the worst cases starving the engine of oil and causing failure as early as 40,000-60,000 km. Over 400,000 vehicles across Europe are affected; the French "Motorgate" class action and a DGCCRF investigation target Renault over this engine, which the company corrected in production in May 2016 but never formally recalled.
records.solution: Renault's procedure is an ECU software update that raises intake manifold pressure to reduce oil ingestion; if consumption remains above 0.25 L/1,000 km the piston rings must be replaced, and severely worn engines need a rebuild or replacement. Owners should check oil every 1,000 km, keep documented top-up records to support goodwill claims, and avoid 2012-2016 cars without service history.
symptoms: Oil level drops noticeably between services (up to 1L per 1,000-1,500 km)
Low oil pressure or oil level warning light
Blue smoke from exhaust, especially on startup
Misfires and rough running from oil-fouled plugs
Loss of power or sudden engine failure in severe cases

records.title: 1.5 dCi DPF/EGR Clogging and AdBlue SCR Faults on Short-Trip Cars
records.description: The 1.5 dCi (K9K) diesel Captur is prone to diesel particulate filter clogging when used mainly for short urban journeys that never let the filter complete an active regeneration; the EGR valve typically sools up at the same time, compounding the airflow restriction. After repeated failed regenerations the ECU forces limp mode with 'Check Anti-Pollution System' warnings. On later Euro 6d Blue dCi versions, AdBlue/SCR faults — injector crystallisation, NOx sensor errors and incorrect urea level readings — additionally trigger 'No start in xxx km' countdown restrictions.
records.solution: A forced regeneration via diagnostic tool or a professional DPF clean usually restores a clogged filter, with EGR valve cleaning or replacement done at the same time; fully blocked filters or failed SCR components (injector, NOx sensor) must be replaced. Prevention is a 20-30 minute sustained-speed motorway run every 300-400 km of urban use and keeping AdBlue topped up with fresh fluid.
symptoms: 'Check Anti-Pollution System' message with engine warning light
Frequent active regenerations (raised idle, cooling fan, hot smell)
AdBlue warning with 'No start in xxx km' countdown (Blue dCi models)

records.title: Cabin Water Ingress Through Door Seals and Blocked Sill Drains
records.description: First-generation Capturs commonly let rainwater into the cabin, most often soaking the rear footwells. The root causes documented across owner forums are thin rear door seals that detach or fail, a poorly designed seal between the bulkhead and the sills, and sill drain (weep) holes that block with dirt — once a sill fills with water it overflows into the floorpan. Left unfixed, standing water under the carpets causes damp smells, persistent window misting, corrosion and faults in underfloor wiring and modules.
records.solution: Trace the entry point with a hose test, then re-seat or replace the failed door weatherstrips, clear the sill weep holes and rubber bungs, and reseal the bulkhead-to-sill joint where needed. Carpets and underlay must be lifted and fully dried to protect wiring and prevent mould.
symptoms: Soaking wet rear passenger footwell carpet after rain
Damp, musty smell and windows misting up inside
Water heard sloshing in the sills or found under sill bungs
Water dripping from the door trim or seal when opening the door
Electrical gremlins from moisture under the carpets

records.title: E-Tech Hybrid Gearbox Input-Shaft O-Ring Oil Leak (155,825-Vehicle Recall)
records.description: On Captur II E-Tech hybrid and plug-in hybrid models, a faulty O-ring seal on the hollow primary shaft of the electric motor inside the DB1 multimode gearbox allows gearbox oil to leak internally. Leaking oil first damages the temperature sensor and, in severe cases, contaminates and overheats the electric motor, causing loss of power or complete loss of drive, with out-of-warranty repairs running €3,000-8,000 for a motor or gearbox replacement. Renault recalled 155,825 E-Tech hybrids built between 5 April 2019 and 26 September 2022 (Clio 5, Captur 2, Arkana, Mégane 4, Dacia Jogger) to check the seal.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers leak-test the hollow primary shaft seal and replace the original O-ring with an improved X-ring seal free of charge (about 30 minutes if no damage has occurred). If oil has already contaminated the electric motor or sensor, the affected components or the complete gearbox must be replaced; cars built after September 2022 have the improved seal from the factory.
symptoms: Gearbox fault or 'Electrical Failure Danger' warning on dashboard
Sudden loss of power or loss of drive while driving
Oil traces under the gearbox/electric motor area
Jerky or inconsistent gear changes from the multimode gearbox

records.title: EDC 6DCT250 Wet Dual-Clutch Shudder and Jerky Engagement
records.description: Captur's EDC (Getrag 6DCT250/DC4) is a wet dual-clutch transmission that develops shudder, hesitation, and jerky engagement after ~50-80k km. Common root causes: degraded clutch oil, worn clutch packs, and TCU software needing reflash. Renault released several software updates and revised oil specifications; symptoms often resolve after fluid service and reflash. Full clutch pack replacement runs €1,500-2,500.
records.solution: Perform EDC clutch adaptation reset via diagnostic tool. Replace the clutch pack assembly if wear is beyond adaptation range. Update the TCU software to the latest calibration.

records.title: Electronic Parking Brake Fails to Auto-Engage — Actuator Sensor Recall (RAPEX 37/2025)
records.description: Captur II vehicles built between 10 April 2024 and 16 January 2025 are covered by an EU safety recall (RAPEX alert 37/2025, ref. SR/03262/25) for an incorrectly angled position sensor inside the electronic parking brake actuator. The misaligned sensor can place the stopping pin incorrectly, so the parking brake does not properly engage when the driver presses P, switches off the engine, releases the seatbelt or opens the door — creating a risk of the vehicle rolling away. The same defect affects the Renault Austral, Mégane E-Tech, Scenic E-Tech, Espace VI and Rafale; the backup Assisted Parking Brake function remains operational.
records.solution: This is a free safety recall: dealers inspect the actuator position sensor alignment and stop-pin position and perform the prescribed corrective action or software update. Owners of affected VINs are contacted by Renault; until the fix, leaving the car in gear and confirming the brake indicator illuminates is advised.
symptoms: Parking brake does not engage automatically when P is selected or engine is switched off
Parking brake warning indicator fails to illuminate after parking
Vehicle creeps or rolls when parked on a slope
Parking brake fault message on instrument cluster

records.title: Infotainment System Glitches
records.description: The second-generation Captur MediaNav and Easy Link infotainment systems suffer from touchscreen freezes, Bluetooth disconnections, and delayed response to inputs. Over-the-air updates sometimes introduce new bugs.
records.solution: Perform a factory reset of the infotainment system. Update to the latest firmware version at the dealer. Clear Bluetooth pairings and re-pair devices. Replace the head unit if hardware failure is confirmed.

records.title: TCe Turbocharger Issues
records.description: The small-displacement TCe turbo engines in the Captur suffer from turbo wastegate rattle and oil seal leaks. The wastegate actuator arm develops play, causing a rattling noise at idle and under light load.
records.solution: Replace the turbo wastegate actuator if rattling. For oil seal leaks, a turbo rebuild or replacement is required. Ensure correct oil specification and change intervals are maintained.

records.title: 1.2 Petrol Valve Cotter Defect — Engine Destruction (DVSA Recall)
records.description: Clio III 1.2 petrol engines built between 17 September and 30 November 2010 were recalled (DVSA reference R/2011/118) because out-of-specification valve cotters could let a valve drop into the cylinder, destroying the engine. 3,308 UK cars were affected. An unremedied car can suffer sudden, catastrophic engine failure with no warning, writing off the engine.
records.solution: The recall remedy is free replacement of the valve cotters by a Renault dealer; owners of 2010-2011 1.2 Clios should check the recall status by VIN on the GOV.UK recall checker. If the failure has already occurred, the engine requires rebuild or replacement.
symptoms: Sudden loud metallic noise from the engine
Immediate engine stall and failure to restart

records.title: 1.5 dCi EGR Valve Sticking and Clogging
records.description: The EGR valve on the 1.5 dCi clogs with soot and carbon, sticking open or closed — a fault so common on this engine that Renault specialists describe 1.5 dCis as suffering 'big time' with EGR problems, and Delphi published a dedicated repair guide for it. A valve stuck open causes rough running, black smoke, and hesitation; stuck closed it raises exhaust gas temperatures, which Honest John forum experts link to consequential turbo bearing failures. The fault commonly logs P2413 (EGR system performance) and recurs if the carbon-packed EGR housing is not also cleaned.
records.solution: Remove and thoroughly clean the EGR valve and its housing of carbon; if the valve is physically worn or its tip has broken off, replace it. Persistent codes after replacement point to EGR wiring, vacuum lines, or the position sensor, which should be checked before fitting another valve.
symptoms: Hesitation or jerky running under load

records.title: 1.5 dCi (K9K) Fuel Injector and Injection Pump Failure
records.description: The 1.5 dCi K9K diesel suffers well-documented fuel injector failures, often triggered by injection pump wear or fuel contamination that sends metal debris through the common-rail system into the injectors. Honest John documented a 2007 Clio 1.5 dCi whose injection pump broke up and sent shards into the injectors, with a repair quote of over £3,600 plus VAT. Owners report sequential injector failures, 'injection fault' dash warnings, power loss, and no-start conditions; once the rail is contaminated, the pump, rail, and all four injectors typically need replacing together.
records.solution: Replace the failed injector(s) with units coded to the ECU and renew the fuel filter; some injectors can be professionally refurbished. If the high-pressure pump has shed debris, the accepted fix is replacing the pump, rail, and all four injectors and flushing the fuel system, otherwise contamination causes repeat failures.
symptoms: Engine shuddering or rough running at idle
Glow plug warning light staying on

records.title: EDC Dual-Clutch Gearbox Judder, TCU Faults and Clutch Failure
records.description: Clio IV models with the six-speed EDC automatic (the dry-clutch Getrag DCT250, the same family as the troubled DSG/PowerShift units) suffer low-speed judder, jerky 1st-2nd shifts, clunks engaging Drive or Reverse, overheating warnings in traffic, and 'Check auto gearbox' messages. Causes range from TCU (transmission control unit) software and module faults — which Renault addressed on some cars — to worn dry-clutch friction surfaces and slow actuators. One documented Clio RS 200 EDC failure drew a quote of about $4,500 for the clutch pack alone.
records.solution: First step is a dealer software update with clutch touch-point relearn and adaptive reset, which cures many judder complaints; TCU replacement fixed others under Renault goodwill. Worn clutch packs or mechatronic faults require replacement of the clutch pack or repair of the mechatronic unit at a gearbox specialist.
symptoms: Judder or shudder when pulling away
Clunking when engaging Drive or Reverse
Gearbox overheating warning in stop-start traffic

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Column Failure
records.description: The electrically assisted steering column on the Clio III (2005-2012) is a notorious failure point: UK steering specialists describe complete column failure as 'a very common fault', caused by poor ground connections to the EPS motor or internal failure of the column's motor and control unit (fault code C1608). Assistance becomes intermittently heavy — sometimes in one direction only — before failing completely, leaving the car drivable but very heavy to steer. The problem resurfaced on the Clio V: a February 2020 EU/DVSA recall covered 2019-built cars for internal failure of the steering column motor control causing loss of assistance while driving.
records.solution: Clean and remake the EPS motor ground connections first; if the column itself has failed, fit a remanufactured or repaired EPS column (around £800 plus VAT and coding for a new unit; remanufactured units are cheaper). Clio V owners should check the DVSA/EU recall status and have the column replaced free by Renault if affected.
symptoms: Steering goes heavy intermittently, sometimes in one direction
'STOP' and steering fault message with total loss of assistance
Vibration through the wheel when turning

records.title: Gearbox Bearing Failure
records.description: The JH3 and JR5 manual gearboxes in the Clio develop differential bearing noise that progressively worsens. The bearings fail from inadequate lubrication at the differential end of the housing.
records.solution: Replace the differential bearings and inspect the crown wheel and pinion for damage. A gearbox oil change with GL-5 75W-80 at 60,000 mile intervals can extend bearing life.

records.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure
records.description: The Clio II and III petrol engines suffer from premature ignition coil pack failure, causing misfires and rough running. The coil packs crack from heat cycling and moisture ingress, particularly on the 1.2 and 1.4 engines.
records.solution: Replace the faulty coil pack. It is recommended to replace all coil packs simultaneously and use OEM Sagem units. Inspect and replace spark plugs at the same time.

records.title: Keycard Not Detected / Card Reader Failure
records.description: Clio III and IV keycard models commonly refuse to start with a 'key card not detected' message. The flexible credit-card-style keycards are bent, sat on, and dropped, eventually killing the internal chip — UK auto locksmiths note both 3- and 4-button cards have a known chip failure — while the in-dash card reader and its antenna ring can also fail and mimic a bad card. Dealership replacement of a single coded card runs roughly €250-400, so owners frequently chase the wrong component without proper diagnosis.
records.solution: Fit a fresh CR2032 battery first, then have a diagnostic check confirm whether the reader actually detects card insertion before buying anything. Replace the failed keycard (auto locksmiths are far cheaper than dealers) or, if the reader is at fault, replace the card reader module.
symptoms: 'Key card not detected' message on the dash
Car fails to start even with a new card battery
Intermittent recognition — card works after reinsertion or wiggling

records.title: TCe Turbo Coolant Leak
records.description: The TCe turbocharged engines develop coolant leaks from the turbocharger coolant lines and the thermostat housing. The plastic coolant connectors become brittle with age and heat exposure, causing seepage and eventual failure.
records.solution: Replace the turbo coolant lines with updated metal fittings where available. Replace the thermostat housing assembly. Pressure test the cooling system after repair to verify no further leaks.

records.title: Timing Belt Tensioner Failure
records.description: The timing belt tensioner bearing on Clio K-series engines can fail before the scheduled belt replacement interval, causing catastrophic engine damage. The water pump, which is driven by the timing belt, also fails prematurely.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt, tensioner, idler pulley, and water pump as a complete kit every 72,000 miles or 5 years, whichever comes first. Do not skip the water pump replacement.

records.title: DPF Regeneration Failure
records.description: The Kadjar diesel models experience frequent DPF regeneration failures, particularly in vehicles used primarily for short urban commutes. The regeneration process requires sustained load that urban driving cannot provide.
records.solution: Perform a forced regeneration via diagnostic tool. Incorporate a weekly 20-minute motorway drive at 2500+ RPM. Clean the DPF pressure differential sensor pipes.

records.title: 2.0 dCi diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage
records.description: The 2.0 dCi diesel Koleos (130/150/175 hp variants) is prone to DPF clogging, especially when driven mainly on short, low-speed trips that never allow the filter to reach regeneration temperature. Symptoms include reduced power / limp mode, visible smoke, and a DPF warning light. Faulty differential pressure or exhaust temperature sensors can worsen or falsely trigger the problem, and a botched dealer forced-regeneration has in some cases destroyed the filter outright.
records.solution: Take the vehicle on periodic longer motorway drives at moderate-to-high RPM to allow passive/active regeneration; verify the differential-pressure and exhaust-temp sensors are working. A clogged filter can often be professionally cleaned (~€100); a destroyed DPF requires replacement (£1,300-£2,000+).

records.title: 2.5 petrol (QR25DE/2TR) timing chain stretch and oil consumption
records.description: The first-generation 2.5-litre petrol Koleos uses the Renault 2TR engine, essentially the Nissan QR25DE. After roughly 100,000-150,000 km many owners experience excessive oil consumption (worn piston rings) and timing chain stretch, often signalled by a rattle on cold start. Delayed oil changes or incorrect oil viscosity accelerate wear of the chain tensioner and guides.
records.solution: Maintain strict oil-change intervals with the correct viscosity and monitor oil level between changes. Investigate any cold-start rattle promptly; a stretched chain requires replacement of the chain, tensioner and guides, and heavy oil burning may need a ring/top-end rebuild.

records.title: AWD rear differential / transfer case internal failure (2.0 dCi 4x4)
records.description: On 2.0 dCi all-wheel-drive Koleos models, the rear differential can fail internally and even crack through its housing, typically between 80,000-100,000 km (sometimes earlier). Owners report oil leaks from the halfshafts and find 1-5mm metal chunks in the differential oil, indicating gear destruction. The failure can recur even after repair if the underlying cause (low oil level / overheating, coupling stress) is not addressed.
records.solution: Check rear differential and transfer-case oil level and condition regularly from around 60,000 km, and change the diff fluid on a strict interval. Inspect for metal contamination early; once gears are damaged the differential (and sometimes the coupling/transfer unit) must be rebuilt or replaced.

Vibration or clunk under AWD load

records.title: X-Tronic CVT transmission failure (slipping, shuddering, high revs)
records.description: The Jatco-sourced X-Tronic CVT used in the Koleos is the single most reported failure point. Owners report gear slipping, shuddering on shifts, hesitation under acceleration, and the engine flaring to high RPM in Drive (belt slip / loss of hydraulic pressure), typically after around 100,000 km. A known contributing cause is the transmission oil cooler allowing engine coolant to mix into the transmission fluid, contaminating and destroying internal components. Complete transmission replacement is common and expensive.
records.solution: Replace CVT fluid every ~60,000-80,000 km (sooner for heavy city/stop-start use) with the correct Renault/Jatco NS-3 spec fluid, and inspect for coolant cross-contamination at the cooler. Early intervention (fluid + cooler) can prevent failure; once the belt/valve body is damaged, a transmission rebuild or replacement is required.

Grinding or whining noise from transmission

records.title: Air Conditioning Failure — Refrigerant Hose Leak and Early Compressor Faults
records.description: A recurring complaint pattern on the Brazilian Kwid: the AC stops cooling because a refrigerant hose routed low near the engine kinks and develops a pinhole leak, slowly venting the gas — the system still appears to work (panel lights, blower runs) but blows warm or only slightly cool air. The hose leak is reported as especially common on 2018 models, and shops frequently misdiagnose it as a simple gas recharge, which fails again within weeks. There is also a cluster of Reclame Aqui complaints about compressors failing very early (one documented at just 20,000 km, cooling only at high RPM) and abnormal noise/vibration when the compressor engages.
records.solution: Have the system leak-tested with UV dye or an electronic sniffer before paying for repeat recharges — check the known trouble spot where the hose runs below/near the engine. Replace the leaking hose and recharge with the correct refrigerant quantity; if the compressor only cools at high RPM or is noisy, test compressor output pressure and replace the compressor if it is worn. On cars still in the 3-year factory warranty, insist on warranty coverage since early compressor failure is well documented.
symptoms: AC blows warm or only slightly cool air
AC only cools at high engine RPM
Noise or vibration when the compressor engages
Refrigerant recharge stops working within weeks
AC gradually loses cooling capacity over months

records.title: Brake Judder and Fade from Undersized Solid Front Discs (Pre-Facelift)
records.description: Pre-facelift Kwids used small 215 mm solid (non-ventilated) front brake discs that overheat under sustained or hard use, leading to fade on long descents and disc warping that owners feel as violent pedal pulsation and steering wheel vibration when braking — often accompanied by metallic noise even with new pads. The trade magazine O Mecânico documents that Renault replaced the solid discs with larger 238 mm ventilated discs in the 2019/2020 line update specifically to improve sustained-braking efficiency and reduce fading; the solid- and ventilated-disc parts (including pads) are not interchangeable. Brake judder remains one of the most commonly cited chronic complaints on early cars in Brazilian owner-problem roundups.
records.solution: On pre-facelift cars with pedal pulsation, replace (not machine) the warped front discs and pads as an axle set — aftermarket ventilated-disc kits for the facelift hub are sold in Brazil, but the straightforward fix is new quality solid discs and pads matched to the original 215 mm spec. Use engine braking on long descents to limit heat buildup. If vibration persists after new discs, have hub runout and wheel bearing seating checked, as improper mounting also causes judder.

Metallic grinding noise even with new pads

records.title: Heavy, Squeaky Clutch and Reverse-Gear Grinding
records.description: The Kwid's cable-operated clutch is a chronic complaint across all model years in Brazil: the pedal becomes heavy and stiff, creaks loudly when pressed (owners compare it to an old door hinge or a trumpet sound when reversing), and reverse gear grinds or refuses to engage. Documented causes are the clutch cable losing lubrication and binding, the release fork deforming, and pressure-plate diaphragm springs weakening — several owners report symptoms starting under 5,000 km, and the local press (Diarinho) covered a case where a dealership dismissed the noise as 'normal.' Vrum additionally documents a smaller number of more severe gearbox failures where first, second, or reverse stop engaging entirely, some within months of purchase.
records.solution: Lubricating the old clutch cable quiets the squeak only for a few days — the documented lasting fix is replacing the clutch kit (disc, pressure plate, release bearing) together with a new clutch cable and checking the release fork for deformation. For hard reverse engagement, fully depress the clutch and pause briefly (or pass through a forward gear first) per Renault's own quick guide; persistent grinding after a new clutch indicates the cable/fork repair was incomplete. Total gearbox failures on cars in warranty should be replaced by Renault under warranty.
symptoms: Loud squeak or creak when pressing the clutch
Difficulty engaging reverse or first gear

records.title: Launch-Era Recall: Brake Component Cracks and Fuel Line Perforation
records.description: In November 2017 Renault do Brasil recalled 21,802 Kwids built between March 1, 2016 and November 2, 2017 (chassis HJ524902 to JJ999218) for two defects announced together. Second, the fuel supply tube was routed/positioned incorrectly and could chafe and perforate, leaking fuel into the engine compartment with fire risk. A related recall in January 2018 covered a batch of September 2017-production cars whose engine cradle (subframe) welds could rupture due to a supplier defect. All campaigns are listed on Renault Brazil's official recall page.
records.solution: Check the chassis number against the recall (Renault Brazil recall portal or 0800 055 5615) and have the recall service performed free of charge at a Renault dealer: inspection and replacement of brake components (up to 1 day) and inspection/repositioning or replacement of the fuel tube (about 1 hour). On any used 2017-2018 Kwid purchase, confirm recall completion — open recalls are still performed at no cost.

records.title: Rear Axle Support Cracking — 2025 Safety Recall (2021-2023 Production)

Brazilian press (Terra, Metrópoles, Autos Segredos) reported the campaign, which also covered some Duster units, and noted it followed an in-depth investigation with local testing — a finding consistent with long-running owner complaints about the rear suspension's fragility on rough Brazilian roads.
records.solution: Check the chassis number on Renault Brazil's recall portal (www.renault.com.br) or call 0800 055 5615 and schedule the free recall service, which began June 5, 2025. The dealer inspects the rear axle support and replaces components as needed; the service takes from 30 minutes up to 8 hours depending on whether replacement is required. Until the recall is performed, have the rear axle mounting points inspected if you hear knocking from the rear or notice handling changes.

records.title: Steering Column Support Bracket Breakage
records.description: One of the most serious and widely reported chronic defects on early Brazilian-market Kwids. The bracket that supports the electric power steering column can crack and break during normal driving, in extreme cases letting the steering wheel drop into the driver's lap with loss of vehicle control. Brazilian outlets (Vrum, Grupo Sentinela, Mundo do Automóvel) document numerous owner reports, concentrated on cars built through 2019, and note that despite the volume of complaints Renault never issued a recall. Dealer quotes reported by owners ranged from roughly R$3,000 to R$5,800 for a complete electric steering column assembly replacement, and several owners only obtained goodwill repairs after escalating publicly.
records.solution: Have the steering column support inspected immediately at any sign of play, clunking, or noise from the column — this is a drive-safety item. The fix is replacement of the column support or, in most documented cases, the complete electric power steering column assembly. Owners of 2017-2019 cars have had partial success obtaining goodwill (cortesia) coverage from Renault Brazil even outside warranty by registering complaints through Renault customer service and Procon/Reclame Aqui; document the defect with photos before repair.
symptoms: Clunking or knocking noise from the steering column
Excessive play or looseness in the steering wheel

Loss of steering control while driving

records.title: 1.5 dCi (K9K) Turbocharger Failure from Oil Starvation
records.description: The K9K 1.5 dCi diesel in the Mégane II and III suffers well-documented turbocharger failures caused by oil starvation: extended oil-change intervals let carbon sludge block the narrow turbo oil feed pipe and sump pickup strainer, starving the turbo bearings. A sticking EGR valve raising exhaust gas temperatures accelerates the bearing failure. Owners report sudden loss of power, a whining turbo and blue smoke; if debris from the failed turbo enters the engine, the bill escalates sharply.
records.solution: Replace the turbocharger together with new oil feed and return pipes, drop the sump to clean the oil pickup strainer, and perform an oil and filter flush — fitting only the turbo guarantees a repeat failure. Stick to shortened oil-change intervals (10,000 km or less) with the correct low-ash C3 oil.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / limp mode, top speed limited to around 60 mph
Whining or siren noise from the turbo
Excessive oil consumption or oil smell near the turbo

records.title: EDC Dual-Clutch Gearbox Judder, Clutch Pack Wear and Mechatronic/TCU Failure (Mégane III/IV)

records.solution: Mild judder is sometimes cured by a TCM/TCU reprogram and adaptation reset; worn clutch packs need replacement (roughly $1,000-2,000), and mechatronic or TCU failures require unit repair or replacement at $1,500-3,000. Keep to Renault's fluid-change and software-update schedule.

records.title: Keycard 'Card Not Detected' and UCH Body Control Module Failures (Mégane II)
records.description: The Mégane II's keycard ignition system and UCH (Unité Centrale Habitacle) body control module are notorious failure points. The transponder coil inside the keycard breaks loose or the dashboard card reader's contacts wear out, while the UCH itself develops internal relay and solder-joint faults. The result is intermittent or total failure to start, plus cascading electrical gremlins because the UCH controls the immobiliser, central locking, wipers, indicators and lights.
records.solution: Replace or repair the keycard (re-solder the transponder coil) and clean or replace the card reader; persistent multi-system faults need the UCH repaired by a specialist (around $65-150 mail-order) or replaced and recoded. Used UCH units must be programmed to the car.

records.title: K9K 1.5 dCi Timing Belt Failure from Misaligned Fuel Pump Pulley
records.description: Renault's K9K 1.5 dCi diesel engine is prone to premature timing belt failure caused by a misaligned high-pressure fuel pump pulley. The pulley's offset rubs the back of the belt, shredding it; when it breaks, the interference engine destroys valves and pistons. Renault revised the pulley design under TSB 04-040 and similar campaigns. Replacement belt + pulley kit runs €400-800 in parts; engine replacement after a snap costs €4,000-8,000.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt kit at reduced intervals (every 60,000 miles). Inspect and replace the front crankshaft seal to prevent oil contamination. Include the water pump in the replacement.

records.title: 1.0 SCe Valve Cover Oil Leak Soaking Spark Plug Wells and Coils
records.description: The 1.0 SCe three-cylinder engine used in the Brazilian Sandero from the 2017 model year has a chronic oil leak at the plastic valve (tappet) cover. The cover's sealing degrades with heat cycles at low mileage — owners on Reclame Aqui describe it as a design defect — and oil seeps into the spark plug wells, soaking the spark plugs and the tips of the ignition coils. This causes misfires, rough running, and repeat fouling of new plugs and coils. Reclame Aqui complaints document leaks appearing on cars with as little as 20,000-30,000 km, sometimes recurring after dealer repair, and related seepage from the timing cover area on the side of the engine. Separately, Renault issued an official recall (service start September 2020) for 1.0-engined units produced July 2019 to January 2020 because a non-conforming oil feed orifice could starve the engine of lubrication, risking seizure or fire — affected owners should confirm completion at a dealer.
records.solution: Replace or reseal the valve cover with an updated gasket/sealant, clean the spark plug wells, and replace oil-fouled spark plugs and any saturated ignition coils. Inspect the timing cover joint at the same time, as it is a secondary leak point on the same engine. The job is inexpensive at an independent shop; the main cost driver is replacement coils if oil has damaged them. For 2020-build cars, check the official Renault recall portal (renault.com.br/recall) for the open oil-feed-orifice lubrication recall, which is repaired free of charge.
symptoms: Oil seepage visible around the valve cover edges
Oil pooled in the spark plug wells when plugs are removed
Oil-fouled spark plugs and oily ignition coil tips
Burning oil smell from the engine bay

records.title: 1.6 8V K7M Head Gasket Failure and Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: Sanderos with the 1.6 8V K7M engine (the workhorse engine of the Brazilian lineup from launch in 2008 through the late 2010s) are widely reported by owners to consume engine oil at an abnormal rate, with the level dropping noticeably between changes and dark smoke from the exhaust. Brazilian repair sources and owner-complaint roundups (Mobiauto, Sua Oficina Online) attribute the recurring cases to a head gasket defect that lets oil pass into the combustion chambers, where it burns with the fuel mixture. Reclame Aqui complaints describe it as a chronic problem, with some owners told the engine was effectively disposable after repeated failures. External oil leaks at the head gasket joint and valve cover are also part of the pattern. Left unaddressed, sustained low oil level risks accelerated wear or engine failure.
records.solution: Check the oil level frequently — every fuel stop on affected cars — and investigate any consumption beyond roughly 0.5 L between services. Confirmed cases require head gasket replacement, with the head checked for flatness and resurfaced if needed; replace valve stem seals while the head is off if smoke persists. A head gasket job on the K7M is mechanically simple and affordable at Brazilian independent shops compared with dealers. Using the correct 10W-40/15W-40 viscosity specified for the K7M matters, since thinner oils worsen consumption on this engine.
symptoms: Oil level dropping rapidly between oil changes
Dark or bluish smoke from the exhaust
Oil residue around the cylinder head gasket joint

records.title: Easy-R Automated Manual Gearbox Clutch and Actuator Failures
records.description: The ZF-supplied Easy-R 5-speed automated manual transmission, offered on Brazilian-market Sandero and Sandero Stepway 1.6 from 2014 production (model years 2015-2019), is one of the most complained-about Renault components on Reclame Aqui. Owners report shuddering and judder when pulling away from a stop appearing as early as 20,000-25,000 km, caused by premature clutch disc wear; failures of the clutch/gear actuator module that leave the car stuck in gear (frequently 2nd) or immobilized; harsh or delayed shifts; and isolated reports of dangerous behavior such as unintended reverse engagement and sudden downshifts at highway speed. Dealer repair quotes have reached R$15,000 (~USD 2,800), with the actuator module alone costing over R$4,400 as a genuine part. Renault discontinued the Easy-R gearbox in Brazil in 2019 after roughly five years on the market, and complaints continued well after the 3-year warranty expired. No recall was ever issued for the gearbox.
records.solution: There is no recall; repairs are owner-paid out of warranty. Premature judder requires replacement of the clutch kit (disc, pressure plate, release bearing) with the updated parts. Actuator faults require recalibration or replacement of the clutch/shift actuator module — independent transmission specialists in Brazil charge roughly half of dealer prices (around R$3,000 vs R$5,500+). After any clutch or actuator work, the system must be relearned/calibrated with a Renault-compatible scan tool (CLIP). Buyers of used 2015-2019 Sandero with Easy-R should test for takeoff shudder and hesitant engagement before purchase, and budget for actuator and clutch service life far shorter than a conventional manual.

records.title: Official Steering Safety Recalls: Ball Joints, Steering Box, and Hydraulic Hose
records.description: Renault Brazil has issued multiple official safety recalls on the Sandero for steering defects, all listed on the manufacturer's recall portal. In 2012, a batch of hydraulic steering boxes (chassis 93YJA1CJ840383-93YJA1CJ932550) had a manufacturing non-conformity that could cause steering malfunction or lock-up. In January 2016, 3,120 Sandero/Logan built November 4 - December 4, 2015 were recalled because non-conforming raw material in the axial ball joints (which connect the steering rack to the wheel ends) could cause the joint to break, resulting in loss of steering control. In November 2017, 13,026 Sandero, Logan, Duster, and Duster Oroch built July 29 - October 6, 2016 were recalled because the power steering low-pressure hose could rupture, leaking fluid and causing steering hardening or loss of assist. A related February 2017 recall covered suspension/steering fastening bolts on 2016-built cars torqued incorrectly, which could deform or break and alter steering behavior. All carry risk of accident with material damage and serious injury.
records.solution: Check whether a specific car is affected by entering the chassis number on Renault Brazil's recall page (renault.com.br/recall) or calling 0800 055 5615, and have any open recall performed free of charge at a Renault dealership — the ball joint inspection/replacement takes about 2.5 hours and the hose replacement about 90 minutes. Recall completion does not expire; used-car buyers should verify these campaigns were performed on 2012 and 2016-2017 model year cars before purchase. Any Sandero with steering play, stiffness, or fluid leaks at the rack should be inspected immediately regardless of recall status.
symptoms: Sudden steering stiffness or heavy steering effort
Power steering fluid leaking under the front of the car
Knocking or play in the steering over bumps
Whining or groaning from the steering pump as fluid is lost
Loss of steering control (ball joint rupture in extreme cases)

records.title: Steering Column Bearing Wear Causing Play and Knocking in the Steering Wheel
records.description: Sandero and its Logan twin suffer a chronic wear problem in the steering column's upper bearing. As the bearing wears, the steering wheel develops perceptible free play and a knocking or clunking sensation, felt especially over rough Brazilian pavement and during small corrections around center. Multiple independent Brazilian mechanic channels document the failure across both generations — including cars as recent as the 2020 Logan — and consistently call it a 'defeito crônico' of the platform. Dealers have been known to quote replacement of the complete steering column, but the documented root cause is just the column bearing, a cheap part. While mostly a nuisance, pronounced play degrades steering precision and several mechanics flag it as an accident risk if ignored long-term.
records.solution: Confirm the diagnosis by checking for free rotation play at the steering wheel with the front wheels held still — wear in the column bearing produces play and noise at the column itself rather than at the rack or tie rods (rule those out first, especially on cars covered by the steering recalls). Replace the steering column upper bearing; the part costs little and the job is a few hours' labor at an independent shop. Replacing the entire column assembly is unnecessary in the typical case and should only be needed if the shaft splines or tube are themselves damaged.
symptoms: Free play in the steering wheel before the wheels respond
Knocking or clunking felt in the steering wheel over bumps
Clicking or rattling noise from the steering column
Noise when shaking the wheel with the car parked

records.title: dCi Diesel Injector Copper Washer Leak
records.description: Renault's K9K and M9R dCi diesel engines used in Scenic II/III/IV develop weeping injector seals as the copper crush washers fatigue with heat cycling. Diesel sweats around the injector body, often coating the head with soot/oil mix and seeping toward the head gasket fire ring. Replacement washers are cheap (€2-5 each) but require careful torquing per Renault procedure; ignored leaks eventually cause cylinder head damage requiring decoke or head rebuild.
records.solution: Replace the copper injector sealing washers and clean the injector seats. If the injector body is leaking, replace the injector. Use a torque wrench to tighten to the correct specification.

records.title: Electric Parking Brake Failure
records.description: The Scenic electric parking brake system is a well-known failure point, with the motor-on-caliper units seizing or the control module losing communication. The brake may apply unexpectedly or fail to release.
records.solution: Replace the parking brake motor on the affected caliper. Update the parking brake ECU software. If both sides are affected, replace both caliper motors simultaneously.

records.title: 12V Battery Discharge and No-Start
records.description: A very common Twizy fault is discharge or failure of the small 12V auxiliary battery, which prevents the vehicle from waking up its control modules and closing the main traction battery contactors. Owners report the car appearing completely dead, showing charging faults, or refusing to select drive after sitting unused; the issue is often caused by an aging AGM battery, parasitic drain, or long storage without a maintainer.
records.solution: Diagnosis starts with checking resting 12V voltage and load-testing the auxiliary battery; anything significantly below about 12.4V after charging usually points to replacement. Inspect battery terminals, ground points, and DC-DC charging operation, then replace the 12V battery if weak; typical battery cost is about $80-$180, with total repair usually $100-$250 including labor. If the battery repeatedly goes flat, owners also check for charger/DC-DC faults and use a maintenance charger during storage.
symptoms: Charging session will not start or stops early
Dashboard warning lights or blank display
Clicking from contactors with no startup

communityRecommendations.content: Keep the 12V battery on a smart maintainer if the Twizy sits for more than a week or two, especially in cold weather.
Owners commonly recommend a quality AGM replacement battery because the Twizy is sensitive to low auxiliary voltage and cheap batteries tend to fail early.
After replacing the battery, clean and tighten the terminals and chassis ground to avoid repeat low-voltage faults.

claims.content: Owners commonly recommend a quality AGM replacement battery because the Twizy is sensitive to low auxiliary voltage and cheap batteries tend to fail early.

records.title: Door, Window, and Latch Water Ingress Problems
records.description: The Twizy's half-door and open-sided design makes it prone to water ingress, rattles, and latch wear. Owners report rain entering around the optional side windows and doors, difficulty latching or opening the scissor doors, and increased cabin noise from worn seals and misadjusted hardware.
records.solution: Inspect door hinges, latch alignment, striker position, and the condition of seals and window panels. Repairs usually involve adjusting the latch/striker, replacing worn seals or fasteners, and lubricating hinges and locks; costs are often $50-$250 for adjustment and minor parts, but damaged door hardware can push repairs toward $400 or more.
symptoms: Door difficult to latch or open

communityRecommendations.content: Regularly lubricate the door hinges and latch mechanisms, especially if the vehicle is parked outdoors.
Owners often use universal automotive weatherstrip material to improve sealing around optional side windows and reduce rattles.
Adjust the striker before replacing the latch, because many hard-closing doors are simply out of alignment.

claims.content: Owners often use universal automotive weatherstrip material to improve sealing around optional side windows and reduce rattles.

records.title: On-Board Charger Failure or Charge Interruption
records.description: Twizy owners frequently report charging faults where the car will not begin charging, stops partway through, or shows a charging system warning. The problem is commonly linked to the on-board charger, charging cable/inlet issues, moisture intrusion, or low 12V system voltage preventing the charger and battery management system from operating correctly.
records.solution: Diagnosis involves confirming mains supply quality, inspecting the integrated charge cable and plug for heat damage, checking the charge inlet and wiring for corrosion, and scanning Renault-specific EV modules for charger faults. Repairs range from cleaning connections or replacing the charge cable components to replacing the on-board charger assembly; minor fixes may cost $150-$400, while charger replacement can run roughly $1,000-$2,500 depending on parts source and labor.
symptoms: Charging stops before battery is full
Plug or cable gets unusually warm
Vehicle remains at low state of charge despite being plugged in

communityRecommendations.content: Check the 12V battery first before condemning the charger, because low auxiliary voltage can mimic a major charging fault.
Owners recommend using a quality replacement charge lead or connector components when heat damage or intermittent charging is found.
Inspect the charge plug and inlet regularly for moisture, corrosion, or discoloration from overheating.

claims.content: Owners recommend using a quality replacement charge lead or connector components when heat damage or intermittent charging is found.

records.title: Battery Capacity Degradation
records.description: The Zoe battery pack experiences capacity degradation that reduces usable range over time. Early 22kWh packs are most affected, with some owners reporting 20-30% capacity loss within 5 years. Frequent rapid charging and high ambient temperatures accelerate degradation.
records.solution: Monitor battery health via the Renault Z.E. app or OBD diagnostic tool. Avoid frequent rapid charging and keep charge between 20-80% for daily use. Battery lease customers can request replacement when capacity drops below 75%.

records.title: Charging System Failure
records.description: The Zoe Chameleon charger experiences intermittent charging failures, refusing to start or stopping mid-charge. The on-board charger module overheats during high-power AC charging, and connector pin corrosion causes communication errors.
records.solution: Clean the charging port connector pins. Check for software updates to the Chameleon charger module. Replace the on-board charger unit if it consistently overheats or refuses to charge.
